evidence.claim: Kpler reported that China announced a full sulphuric-acid export ban through August 2026, replacing a 700,000-tonne annual quota with a complete cessation, with Chile, Indonesia, and Saudi Arabia identified as primary 2026 destination markets.

evidence.claim: Kpler reported that Indonesian HPAL capacity imports approximately 75-80% of its sulphur from the Middle East Gulf and that Indonesian buyers are sourcing sulphuric acid from Japan and Korea, competing with Chilean copper producers for smelter-acid byproduct supply.

evidence.claim: ORF reported that China prohibited sulphuric-acid exports from May 1, 2026 and shipped approximately 4.6 million metric tonnes of sulphuric acid in 2025.

summary: Layer 2B maps the visible candidate chunk into ticker-to-node relationships. The strongest mapped relationships in this chunk are AI-server passive-component exposure through Japanese reference leaders and underfollowed component suppliers, plus separate hypothesis lanes for automotive aluminum sheet disruption and HALEU/nuclear fuel. Because the external evidence supplied to this call is concentrated in sulphur/sulphuric-acid and InP substrate chokepoints, most MLCC, T-glass, aluminum, and nuclear relationships remain hypotheses or inferences until verified with company filings, product disclosures, customer evidence, order/backlog commentary, and market-pricing checks. No buy/sell recommendation is made.
